questions.prompt: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
options: Energy is never created or destroyed — it only changes form
Energy disappears when objects slow down
Machines can make energy from nothing
Energy always runs out eventually
questions.explanation: The total stays constant; energy only trades between forms like motion, height, heat, and sound.
questions.misconception: People think energy vanishes when something stops; it has only changed form.

questions.prompt: A ball rolls off a ramp at the top of a slope. Which energy swap happens as it descends?
options: Potential (height) changes into kinetic (motion)
Kinetic changes into potential all the way down
Light changes into sound
Nothing changes — energy is frozen
questions.explanation: Down the slope, stored height energy converts into motion — the same total, a different form.
questions.misconception: The reverse swap (motion to height) is what happens climbing up, not descending.

questions.prompt: Where does a braking car's kinetic energy go?
options: Mostly into heat in the brakes and tyres
Into nothing — it is gone forever
Into extra fuel the engine just gained
It stays in the wheels forever
questions.explanation: Friction turns motion into heat; energy is conserved, so it hasn't vanished — it warmed things up.
questions.misconception: The 'it just disappears' intuition ignores heat, the most common energy destination.

questions.prompt: In a closed system, the total energy...
options: Stays the same at every moment
Grows as work is done
Shrinks as the object tires
Doubles at the top of a hill
questions.explanation: By definition a closed system has no energy entering or leaving, so the sum is fixed.
questions.misconception: Counting only the visible form (motion) and forgetting heat makes totals seem to shrink.

questions.prompt: At any moment while the coaster loops, which of these is true?
options: PE + KE + heat = the same starting total
PE is always larger than the total
KE must be zero at the bottom
The total halves after each loop
questions.explanation: Every form adds to the same constant — that sum is the law in one line.
questions.misconception: Focusing on just one form makes the total look like it changes; all forms must be added.
